assumptions.allowance: Synthetic. A capacity-1 account has 500 units per five-hour window and 5000 per weekly window; capacity scales both linearly. Real allowances are not published.
assumptions.windows: Synthetic. Five-hour and weekly windows reset on a fixed schedule from the fixture start; real five-hour windows start at first use.
assumptions.cost: Synthetic. One unit is 1000 weighted tokens: uncached input 1, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, output 5. These are API price ratios, used only as a stand-in for allowance consumption.
assumptions.cache: Synthetic. A prompt prefix stays cached for 5 minutes after its last use, per account and conversation. A request on another account while the old cache is warm counts its prefix as a migration write.
assumptions.observations: Every response reports exact utilization and resets.
assumptions.external_load: acct-y loses 5% of its five-hour allowance per hour to clients outside this proxy, so its observations age quickly.
assumptions.overage: A settings read finds paid overflow disabled on every account every 15 minutes.
assumptions.load: About 70% of the pool's five-hour allowance. acct-w and acct-x hold most of their weekly allowance and reset within the run; acct-y and acct-z reset after it.
assumptions.faults: 1% transient failures before output; no partial streams, cancellations, logouts, or restarts.
